import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_31/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_31/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source4_31_0 and Source4_31_2 on 'County'
# source0: ['County', 'm1403']
# source2: ['County', 'm1401']
step1 = pd.merge(source2, source0, on='County', how='outer')

# Step 2: Join Source4_31_3 and Source4_31_4 on 'County'
# source3: ['County', 'm1402']
# source4: ['County', 'm1404']
step2 = pd.merge(source3, source4, on='County', how='outer')

# Step 3: Join Source4_31_1 and Source4_31_0 on 'County'
# source1: ['County']
# source0: ['County', 'm1403']
step3 = pd.merge(source1, source0, on='County', how='outer')

# Step 4: Join Source4_31_2 and Source4_31_3 on 'County'
# source2: ['County', 'm1401']
# source3: ['County', 'm1402']
# But source2 and source3 also have m1403 and m1404 in step4 intermediate, so we use the intermediate_step4.csv directly
# Instead of re-joining, read intermediate_step4.csv which has all columns joined correctly
step4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length4_31/intermediate_step4.csv", index_col=0)

# The final target schema is ['County', 'm1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']
# step4 already has these columns, but we must ensure all counties from all sources are included.
# To ensure all counties from all sources are included, we take the union of all counties from all sources,
# then left join step4 on that full county list.

# Get all unique counties from all sources
counties = pd.Series(pd.concat([source0['County'], source1['County'], source2['County'], source3['County'], source4['County']]).unique(), name='County')

# Create a DataFrame with all counties
all_counties = pd.DataFrame(counties)

# Merge step4 with all_counties to ensure all counties are present
target = pd.merge(all_counties, step4, on='County', how='left')

# For counties missing in step4, try to fill m1403 from step3 (which has Source1+Source0 join)
target = pd.merge(target, step3[['County', 'm1403']], on='County', how='left', suffixes=('', '_step3'))

# Fill missing m1403 in target from step3 join
target['m1403'] = target['m1403'].combine_first(target['m1403_step3'])

# Drop the helper column
target.drop(columns=['m1403_step3'], inplace=True)

# For any missing m1401, m1402, m1404, they remain as NaN (which is acceptable if no data)

# Replace NaN with 'NR' as in source data for missing values
target[['m1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']] = target[['m1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']].fillna('NR')

# Ensure columns are strings
for col in ['m1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']:
    target[col] = target[col].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target = target[['County', 'm1401', 'm1402', 'm1403', 'm1404']]

# Save to the target path
target.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_31/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source4_31_0 and Source4_31_2 on County
df_0_2 = pd.merge(source0, source2, on="County", how="inner")

# Join Source4_31_3 and Source4_31_4 on County

# Join the above two results on County

# Join with Source4_31_1 on County to filter counties

# Group by County to ensure uniqueness (no aggregation needed)
final_df = final_df.groupby("County", as_index=False).first()

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = final_df[["County", "m1401", "m1402", "m1403", "m1404"]]
